title: Best Phone Under 25000 in Bangladesh
summary: Compare the 10 best phones under 25000 taka in Bangladesh. See display, chipset, camera, and battery specs, plus who should buy each phone.
intro: Find the best phone under 25000 in Bangladesh with big batteries, smooth screens, and good cameras.
html:
Most Bangladeshi mobile phone users start their smartphone journey with an affordable phone that offers a 5-inch display, balanced performance, a decent camera, and a max 3500 mAh battery. That was enough for calls, Facebook, and YouTube a few years ago.

Today, even an affordable mobile phone under 25000 taka is expected to do much more. We now expect a 6.5-inch or larger display with a smooth 90Hz or 120Hz refresh rate, a large battery that lasts a full day, fast charging, at least 6GB or 8GB of RAM, and a 50MP camera that works well even in low light. Many people also want 5G support and software updates that keep the phone useful for years.

Not long ago, phones under 25000 offered most of these features. But since the global memory chip shortage, consumer electronics prices have risen all over the world, as well as mobile phones. To get similar specs, you now need to pay 5000 to 10000 taka more than before.

But don’t lose hope. The best phones under 25000 in Bangladesh are still available from popular brands, including Tecno, HONOR, Redmi, Realme, Samsung, ZTE, and Infinix. In this blog, we will list the top 10 best phone under 25000, so you can pick the right one without wasting your time and money.

Top 10 Best Phone Under 25000 in Bangladesh

Every phone below costs under 25000 and has a 90Hz or 120Hz screen, a battery of 5000 mAh or more, and a 50MP or better main camera, with one exception. Some are built for battery life, some for selfies, and one comes with Samsung’s official support. At Star Tech, each best phone on this list has the key specifications and who should buy the mobile phone, so you can compare them quickly. Pick the one feature you need most, and let the rest follow.

Tecno SPARK 50 Pro

The Tecno SPARK 50 Pro suits people who drain their phone on heavy days and want a quick recharge. Its 6000 mAh battery supports 60 W fast charging, so a short charge gives hours of use. The Helio G100 Ultimate handles daily apps and popular mobile games like Free Fire, PUBG, and COD Mobile without stuttering. The Tecno phone's 120 Hz IPS display keeps scrolling, and the video is smooth.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.78-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G100 Ultimate (6nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 256GB internal storage
  • Camera: 50MP main rear camera, 8MP front camera
  • Battery and Charging: 6000 mAh with 60 W fast charging
  • Features: Side fingerprint scanner, DTS audio, MicroSD slot

Who Should Buy the Tecno SPARK 50 Pro?

Commuters, students, and field workers will like the Tecno SPARK 50 Pro battery life and fast charging between shifts and gaming. The 256GB storage helps if you keep videos offline. Camera enthusiasts may find the single 50MP lens limiting.

HONOR X6e

The HONOR X6e is built around a 7500mAh battery. Moderate users can stretch it close to two days. The Helio G81 Ultra sips power and keeps the 120Hz TFT display responsive. At 6.61 inches, this Honor phone display is smaller than most rivals here, so one-handed use is easier. MagicOS adds some useful productivity features without much bloat.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.61-inch HD+ TFT LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G81 Ultra (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 6GB RAM / 128GB storage
  • Camera: 50MP main rear camera, 5MP front camera
  • Battery and Charging: 7500mAh with 45W fast charging
  • Features: MagicOS 8.0, side fingerprint, face unlock

Who Should Buy the HONOR X6e?

Travelers and delivery riders who are often away from a power outlet will get the HONOR X6e most from the battery. The smaller body also suits anyone who finds 6.7-inch phones too big. Heavy gamers should look at a stronger chipset.

Redmi 17

The Redmi 17 has a 6.9-inch 120Hz display, which works well for videos, reading, and social feeds. The 7500mAh battery keeps that large screen running through the day. The Helio G91 Ultra gives steady performance for daily apps and light gaming. This Xiaomi phone's auxiliary rear lens helps with depth effects in portraits.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.9-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G91 Ultra (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 256GB storage
  • Camera: Dual 50MP + auxiliary lens rear, 8MP front
  • Battery and Charging: 7500mAh with 45W fast charging
  • Features: Xiaomi HyperOS, IR blaster, 3.5mm jack, MicroSD

Who Should Buy the Redmi 17?

If you stream a lot or read on your phone, the Redmi 17 big screen is the main draw. The IR blaster also lets you control a TV or AC. People with small hands or tight pockets may find it too large.

Realme C100x

The Realme C100x has the biggest battery on this list at 8000 mAh. Light users can expect close to three days between charges. The Unisoc T7250 focuses on efficiency, which helps the battery last. The 6.8-inch 120Hz IPS panel looks smooth, and Realme UI stays clean. This Realme phone's rear cameras cover main and depth shots well enough.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.8-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: Unisoc T7250 (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 128GB storage
  • Camera: Dual 50MP + auxiliary lens rear, 5MP front
  • Battery and Charging: 8000mAh with 45W fast charging
  • Features: Realme UI 5.0, side fingerprint, MicroSD

Who Should Buy the Realme C100x?

Choose this Realme C100x if battery life matters more than anything else. It fits people in areas with limited charging access and anyone who wants one phone that rarely needs a charger. Gamers should pick a stronger processor.

Samsung Galaxy A07

The Samsung Galaxy A07 comes with Samsung's official Bangladesh warranty and six years of security updates. The Helio G99 (6 nm) runs efficiently and stays steady under sustained app use and gaming. The 90Hz PLS LCD gives decent motion clarity. One UI Core keeps this Samsung phone interface clean and free of ads. The 50MP + 2MP rear cameras take reliable everyday photos.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.7-inch HD+ PLS LCD with 90Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G99 (6nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 6GB RAM / 128GB storage
  • Camera: Dual 50MP + 2MP rear, 8MP front
  • Battery and Charging: 5000 mAh with 25 W fast charging
  • Features: One UI Core 6, Samsung Knox, 6 years of security updates

Who Should Buy the Samsung Galaxy A07?

First-time smartphone buyers and parents buying for teenagers should look at the Samsung Galaxy A07 first. The same goes for anyone who wants long security support and easy repairs. Heavy gamers and video watchers may want a faster screen and quicker charging.

ZTE nubia V80 Pro

The ZTE nubia V80 Pro has a 108MP main sensor, which captures more detail than the usual 50MP camera. Its 16MP front camera is also the sharpest selfie option on this best phone list. The Unisoc T7280 handles image processing, and the 120Hz IPS display makes this ZTE phone viewfinder smooth. The 5000mAh battery with 22.5W charging covers a full day of mixed use.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.75-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: Unisoc T7280 (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 256GB storage
  • Camera: Dual 108MP + auxiliary lens rear, 16MP front
  • Battery and Charging: 5000mAh with 22.5W fast charging
  • Features: nubia UI, side fingerprint, Hi-Res audio

Who Should Buy the ZTE nubia V80 Pro?

Pick the ZTE Nubia V80 Pro if you want high-resolution stills under this price point for cropping or printing. Social media creators who post selfies will also like the 16MP front camera. Video creators and gamers need a stronger video processor.

Tecno SPARK 50C

The Tecno SPARK 50C is for buyers who want a working modern phone at the lowest price. The 120Hz IPS display and Helio G81 handle messaging, calls, and light browsing smoothly. The 5200mAh battery with 15W charging covers daily needs. The 13MP main camera is fine for document scans and casual photos.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.78-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G81 (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 4GB RAM / 128GB storage
  • Camera: 13MP rear camera, 8MP front camera
  • Battery and Charging: 5200mAh with 15W charging
  • Features: HiOS 14, side fingerprint, DTS sound

Who Should Buy the Tecno SPARK 50C?

Students on a tight budget, seniors who want a simple smartphone, and people who need a backup device will find Tecno SPARK 50C enough. The 120Hz display feels better than most entry-level screens. Multitaskers and photo lovers should spend more.

Infinix Hot 70

The Infinix Hot 70 sits in the middle of this best phone list. It has the Helio G100 Ultimate (6 nm), a 6000 mAh battery, and 45 W charging. The 120Hz IPS display keeps this Infinix phone interface smooth. The 50MP main camera takes decent photos in good light. XOS 14 offers customization options that are easy for new users.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.78-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G100 Ultimate (6nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 256GB storage
  • Camera: 50MP rear camera, 8MP front camera
  • Battery and Charging: 6000mAh with 45W fast charging
  • Features: XOS 14, in-display fingerprint, Dual speakers

Who Should Buy the Infinix Hot 70?

This Infinix Hot 70 works for anyone who wants a reliable all-rounder without a standout feature. The IP54 rating helps outdoors, and the dual speakers mean you can skip headphones. Macro photography or heavy gaming needs a different phone.

ZTE nubia V80 Design

The ZTE nubia V80 Design is slim, and its 16MP front camera suits selfies and video calls. The Unisoc T7280 and 120Hz IPS display run daily tasks smoothly. The rear cameras cover standard and depth shots. The 5000mAh battery with 22.5W charging handles a normal day.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.75-inch HD+ IPS LCD with 120Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: Unisoc T7280 (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 8GB RAM / 256GB storage
  • Camera: Dual 50MP + auxiliary lens rear, 16MP front
  • Battery and Charging: 5000mAh with 22.5W fast charging
  • Features: nubia UI, side fingerprint, slim bezels

Who Should Buy the ZTE nubia V80 Design?

If you want a phone that looks and feels premium, the ZTE nubia V80 Design glass back and thin body deliver. It also suits people who take many selfies or make video calls. Anyone worried about battery life should choose a thicker phone.

HONOR X5c Plus

Do you want a simple phone from a known brand, without paying for features you will not use? The HONOR X5c Plus fits that idea. Its 6.74-inch screen runs at 90Hz, so scrolling feels smoother than on a basic 60Hz panel. The Helio G81 handles chats, social media, and video calls. The 5260mAh battery covers a normal day, and the 3.5mm jack keeps wired earphones useful.

Key Specifications:

  • Display: 6.74-inch HD+ TFT LCD with 90Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Helio G81 (12nm)
  • RAM and Storage: 4GB RAM / 128GB storage
  • Camera: 50MP main rear camera with auxiliary lens, 5MP front camera
  • Battery and Charging: 5260 mAh with 15 W charging
  • Features: Android 15 with MagicOS 9, side fingerprint, 3.5mm jack, MicroSD

Who Should Buy the HONOR X5c Plus?

Anyone upgrading from an old phone will find the HONOR X5c Plus easy to live with. The microSD slot and headphone jack help if you store music and videos offline. Charging at 15W is slow, and 4GB RAM limits heavy multitasking, so gamers should look higher.

Which Phone Under 25000 Is Right for You?

Start with the problem you face most often. If you hate charging daily, the Realme C100x or HONOR X6e solves it. If you want photos worth printing, the ZTE nubia V80 Pro has the resolution. If you game on your commute, the Tecno SPARK 50 Pro charges faster than the Helio G100 Ultimate phones. The Infinix Hot 70 uses the same chipset with 45W charging. If you keep phones for years, the Samsung Galaxy A07 offers security updates and official repairs. If you watch videos on the go, pick the Redmi 17 for the 6.9-inch screen. If you want a simple phone with a headphone jack and microSD slot, the HONOR X5c Plus keeps things basic.
